title: Paramedic officer
description: Review (medicines, IV, intubation) + breathing patterns, CPR medicines and procedures, ECG rhythms: shockable or not.

questions.q: Wheezing, the patient can only speak in short words. What do you think of?
answers: A severe asthma attack
Pulmonary oedema
A panic attack with hyperventilation
A blocked airway from a foreign body

questions.q: Crackles, swollen ankles, pink frothy sputum. What is it and what is the treatment?
answers: Pulmonary oedema: sit up, Nitroglycerin, oxygen
Pneumonia: oxygen, lying flat, fluid through the IV
Pulmonary oedema: lie flat, raise the legs, fluid IV
Severe asthma: sit up, Salbutamol nebulised, oxygen

questions.q: Deep, fast breathing with an acetone smell on the breath?
answers: Ketoacidosis, very high blood glucose
Hypoglycaemia, very low blood glucose
Alcohol poisoning with a full stomach
Hyperventilation caused by panic

questions.q: Slow, shallow breathing. What does it point to?
answers: Opioid or sleeping pill poisoning
Exhaustion after a long asthma attack only
Ketoacidosis with a very high glucose
Stimulant (cocaine, amphetamine) overdose

questions.q: Snoring breathing in an unconscious patient?
answers: Partial airway obstruction: the airway must be secured
Deep sleep after a seizure: let them rest and watch
Wheezing from narrowed airways: Salbutamol is needed
Fluid in the lungs: sit the patient up, give Nitro

questions.q: What does gasping (agonal) breathing mean?
answers: A sign of cardiac arrest: start CPR
The patient breathes, so no CPR is needed
Hyperventilation: calm the patient down
Partial airway block: tilt the head only

questions.q: COPD patient, pursed lips, sitting leaning forward. What helps the most?
answers: Oxygen (Salbutamol less)
Only Salbutamol, oxygen is dangerous
Nitroglycerin spray and sitting up
Lying flat so the patient can rest

questions.q: Which rhythm is this, and is it shockable?
answers: Ventricular fibrillation, shockable
Ventricular tachycardia, not shockable
Fine VF that looks like asystole, not shockable
PEA, shockable with synchronised mode

questions.q: Which rhythms are shockable?
answers: VF and pulseless VT
VF and asystole
Pulseless VT and PEA
Asystole and PEA

questions.q: What do you do in asystole?
answers: CPR and Adrenaline as soon as possible, no shock
CPR and a shock, because there is no rhythm at all
CPR, and Adrenaline only after the third cycle
CPR and Amiodarone, then shock if it changes

questions.q: What is PEA?
answers: Electrical activity without a pulse: CPR, Adrenaline, look for the cause
Fast chaotic activity without a pulse: shock it, then CPR and Adrenaline
A slow rhythm with a weak pulse: watch it and give oxygen only
A rhythm with a pulse: synchronised cardioversion, then monitoring

questions.q: In a shockable rhythm, when do you give the first Adrenaline?
answers: After the 3rd shock
After the 1st shock
Before the 1st shock
After the 5th shock

questions.q: What becomes of untreated ventricular fibrillation within a few minutes?
answers: It turns into asystole, the chance of survival keeps falling
It turns into VT with a pulse, so the patient may wake up
It usually returns to sinus rhythm if CPR is done well
It turns into PEA, which is easier to treat than VF

questions.q: Why do we not shock a normal sinus rhythm?
answers: The shock can stop the heart
The shock would burn the skin badly
The rhythm is too slow for a shock
The pads cannot sense a sinus rhythm

questions.q: VT with a pulse, unstable patient. What do you do?
answers: Synchronised cardioversion (SYNC mode)
Unsynchronised shock at full energy
Adrenaline 1 mg IV, then CPR
Start CPR, the pulse will not hold

questions.q: Which belong to the “4H” reversible causes of cardiac arrest?
answers: Hypoxia, hypovolaemia, hypo- / hyperkalaemia, hypothermia
Hypoxia, hypertension, hypo- / hyperglycaemia, hyperthermia
Hypovolaemia, hypotension, hypocalcaemia, haemorrhage
Hypoxia, hypoglycaemia, hypothermia, heart tamponade

questions.q: Besides good quality CPR, what improves the chance of ROSC?
answers: Adrenaline and a secured airway
Captopril and a secured airway
Fast fluid and more breaths
Glucose IV given to everyone

questions.q: How often do the people doing compressions swap?
answers: About every 2 minutes, at the rhythm check
About every 5 minutes, after each Adrenaline
After every 30 compressions, at the breaths
Only when the one doing it gets tired

questions.q: What do you do after ROSC?
answers: Monitor, watch the rhythm and blood pressure, transport: it can stop again
Take off the pads, give oxygen, and transport without the monitor
Give one more shock to keep the rhythm stable, then transport
Give Adrenaline every 3–5 minutes so the heart does not stop again

questions.q: This rhythm is shown and the patient has no pulse. Is it shockable?
answers: No: asystole, CPR and Adrenaline
Yes: fine VF, shock at once
Yes: shock it with SYNC mode
No: check the leads, then wait

questions.q: This rhythm is shown, the patient does not respond and has no palpable pulse. What do you do?
answers: Pulseless VT: shockable, defibrillation and CPR
VT: synchronised cardioversion, then watch the pulse
PEA: not shockable, CPR and Adrenaline only
Fast sinus rhythm: oxygen and fluid, no CPR

questions.q: This rhythm is on the monitor, but there is no palpable pulse on the large arteries. What is it?
answers: PEA: not shockable, CPR and Adrenaline
Sinus rhythm: the pulse is just too weak
PEA: shockable, shock and then CPR
VT with a pulse: synchronised shock

questions.q: The patient talks, has a palpable pulse, and the monitor shows this. What do you do with the defibrillator?
answers: Nothing: sinus rhythm, not shockable
SYNC cardioversion with low energy
Shock once to be safe, then monitor
Attach the pads and charge it to be ready

questions.q: A patient collapsed suddenly and this rhythm is shown. What matters most?
answers: Defibrillation as soon as possible, CPR in between
Adrenaline as soon as possible, shock after 3 cycles
Synchronised cardioversion with low energy at once
Airway and intubation first, then the defibrillation

questions.q: Which rhythm is NOT shockable?
answers: PEA
Ventricular fibrillation
Pulseless ventricular tachycardia
Fine ventricular fibrillation

questions.q: What do you do after a shock?
answers: Continue CPR at once for 2 minutes, only then check the rhythm
Check the pulse and the rhythm at once, CPR only if there is none
Wait 10 seconds for the monitor to analyse the new rhythm
Give Adrenaline at once, then continue CPR for 2 minutes

questions.q: Cardiac arrest caused by hypoglycaemia. What do you give besides CPR?
answers: Glucose 40% IV
Glucose gel by mouth
Fluid IV, quickly
Insulin IV
